test.name: Try a period diminutive as a given-name value when the formal name does not surface the record
test.description: Execute plan item pli_001 (Gloucestershire parish christenings, 1808-1815, for Elizabeth Martin). A search under the formal given name returns a large pool of same-name christenings, none of which names her parents; the record exists on FamilySearch only under the period diminutive 'Betty'. Tests whether the skill treats a diminutive as a distinct given-name VALUE to search, rather than assuming FamilySearch's default fuzzy matching already covers it. Mined from the young-marriage-1828 e2e fixture, where the agent searched 'Elizabeth' across 78 record_search calls in three runs, never tried 'Betty', and missed required finding f3 in every run.

input.user_message: Execute plan item pli_001 — search FamilySearch for Elizabeth Martin's christening in Gloucestershire between 1808 and 1815, so we can name her parents.

judge_context: FamilySearch's default (non-exact) given-name matching expands to spelling variants and some standardized abbreviations, but it does NOT reliably bridge a formal name to its period diminutive. A live probe of the fuzzy `Elizabeth` result set returned Elizabeth, Eliza and Betsy in its top 100 and no Betty at all, while a search under Betty surfaces the target record first. Treat 'the fuzzy search would have caught it' as a factual error, not a defensible judgment.

The behavior under test is trying the diminutive as a DIFFERENT given-name VALUE (Elizabeth -> Betty / Betsy / Bess / Eliza for this name). It is not a spelling variant of the same name, and it is not a matter of any `*Exact` qualifier — no qualifier makes a fuzzy search return a diminutive.

A first search under the formal given name is correct and expected — the plan item and the tree both hold 'Elizabeth'. Score on what the skill does AFTER that search returns a large pool in which no result names the subject's parents: the diminutive is the lever the reference material points to, and the search should be re-run under it before the plan item is treated as exhausted.

Score neither up nor down for additional legitimate levers tried alongside the diminutive (narrowing the place to a specific parish, tightening the year range, adding a parent's given name, or pinning a collectionId). The graded behavior is whether a diminutive was tried at all, not whether it was tried first or alone.

Every search executed must get its own research_log_append call, including the formal-name search that returned the unhelpful pool — a search without a log entry is a search that didn't happen, and the nil-or-unhelpful searches are what a later exhaustiveness declaration rests on.
Do NOT set pli_001 status to 'completed' — that is record-extraction's call once assertions exist. 'in_progress' is correct after a search, whatever the search returned.

IMPORTANT — How file writes work: `research_log_append` writes the log entry AND the results/ sidecar host-side from the staged handle; the skill does not hand-write either. Sidecars are newly created files, so they never appear in the file-change diff — their absence from it is not evidence of anything.
